sentences.text:
This Miscellaneous Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed by the appellants/claimants challenging the award dated 05.03.2004 passed by IInd Additional Member of Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gadarwara (M.P.), in MVC No.37/2003, whereby the Tribunal dismissed the claim petition filed by claimants.
2.
The claimants are the father and mother of deceased Raju aged about 11 years, who was playing in front of his house on 16.12.1999 at about 10:30 in the morning.
3. The factual matrix of the case are that on 16.12.1999 the deceased Raju aged 11 years met with an accident, as a result, he sustained fatal injuries and succumbed to death on the spot.

Therefore,
claimants being his father and mother filed a claim petition claiming compensation to the tune of Rs.3,20,000/-.

4. Respondent no.1 and 2 denied the happening of the accident and also NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:54123 2 MA-1471-2004 pleaded that the vehicle was insured with respondent no.3/ Insurance Co. and it is the liability of the Insurance Co. to pay the compensation.
Respondent no.3 in reply stated that the driver of the vehicle was not having the licence and there was violation of terms and condition of insurance policy.
Therefore, the Insurance Co. cannot be held liable to pay the compensation.

5. After appreciation of the evidence on record, the learned Claims Tribunal dismissed the entire claim on the ground that the claimants failed to prove that the accident occurred with the vehicle in question and the accident was caused by respondent no.1 due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: Counsel for appellant after arguing at length submitted that the impugned award is contrary to law and the learned Tribunal took the matter in casual manner.
It is further submitted that the Tribunal fell in error in not properly appreciating the oral and documentary evidence pleaded by the claimants.
7. After hearing the rival submissions and upon perusal of the records of the Tribunal, this Court finds that the Tribunal has not committed any error of law in dismissing the claim petition.
In the present case, the appellant examined PW-1 Ramesh Chouksey and PW-2 Rakesh, who is stated to be an eyewitness to the accident.
However, there are several contradictions in their testimonies recorded before the Tribunal.
It is also pertinent to note that the claimants have not correctly arrayed the name of the owner of the offending vehicle as a party to the proceedings.

Upon appreciation of the evidence on record, the Tribunal rightly held that it was incumbent upon the claimant to NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:54123 3 MA-1471-2004 establish the vehicle number, the identity of the driver and owner, and that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the said driver.
However, Rakesh, the eyewitness of applicants' stated that the deceased child Raju was playing on the road.

In the given circumstances, it has not been established which vehicle number was involved in the collision, nor has it been proved that the driver, Dashrath,
was driving the alleged offending vehicle, a Tata Sumo Jeep, at a high speed or in a rash and negligent manner.
On the contrary, the evidence on record establishes that the deceased child was playing on the road at the time of the incident, and therefore, the driver cannot be held responsible for the accident.
8. The findings recorded by the learned Tribunal cannot be said to be perverse or based on any misreading of the evidence of PW-1 and PW-2.
In the facts and circumstances of the case, the conclusion arrived at by the Tribunal was inevitable and has been rightly reached.

There is,
therefore, no scope for interference with the findings of the Tribunal in this appeal.
9. Accordingly, in view of the foregoing discussion, the appeal fails and is hereby dismissed.

(HIMANSHU JOSHI) JUDGE rv Ramesh Kumar & Anr vs Dashrath & Ors on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57692293/
